correctness.rationale: The Finding attributes independent 2+Geom(1/2) complete-arch lengths to the finite uniform length-n word. Literally these are stopped by the observation horizon: for n=3, conditional on having a complete arch its length is 3 with probability one, not 1/2. The proof's intended interpretation is correct: in an infinite chain, an arch first sees two distinct symbols in two draws, then discovers the third with conditional probability 1/2 at each draw. The law at each boundary is independent of the boundary letter by symmetry, yielding iid durations on the infinite chain; I_n counts their partial sums at most n. Greedy arches characterize fixed-alphabet universality by the last-first-appearance obstruction, explaining why omitted symbols yield index zero. The binomial tail is the probability of at least k successes in n−2k fair trials. Using A(x)=x³/(2−x), the probability GF is (1−A)/[(1−x)(1−uA)], which gives F after converting prefix probabilities to counts. The renewal CLT gives variance rate 2/4³ and the LLN gives 1/4. Independent principal-part calculations for the mean and second factorial-moment GFs at t=1−x give 1/(4t²)−9/(16t) and 1/(8t³)−9/(16t²)+115/(128t); the other poles are at modulus sqrt(2). This confirms −5/16, 13/256 and both error terms. Thus the distribution and limit formulas are correct under the intended coupling; the as-stated law of finite completed arches is not.
